ja: アルキメデスは「てこ」の法則を数学的に説明し、「立つ場所があれば地球も動かしてみせる」と言ったと伝えられる。
easy: Archimedes explained how a long stick can lift heavy things. He said, 'Give me a place to stand, and I will move the Earth.'
std: Archimedes described the law of the lever mathematically and is said to have declared, 'Give me a place to stand, and I will move the Earth.'

ja: 人の体には約37兆個の細胞があり、腸などにすむ細菌もほぼ同じくらいの数（約38兆個）いると推定されている。
easy: Your body has about 37 trillion cells. About the same number of very small living things live inside you too.
std: The human body has roughly 37 trillion cells, and recent estimates suggest about the same number of bacteria live in and on us.

ja: 人は1日に1万回以上まばたきをする。目を閉じている時間を合計すると、起きている間に数十分になる。
easy: We close and open our eyes more than 10,000 times a day. All together, our eyes are closed for many minutes each day.
std: People blink more than 10,000 times a day, which adds up to many minutes of closed eyes during waking hours.

ja: 脳の重さは体重の約2%だが、体が使うエネルギーの約20%を使っている。
easy: The brain is only about 2% of your body weight, but it uses about 20% of your energy.
std: The brain makes up about 2% of body weight but uses around 20% of the body's energy.

ja: 大人の骨は約206本だが、赤ちゃんは約300本ある。成長するにつれて骨がくっついて数が減る。
easy: An adult has about 206 bones, but a baby has about 300. Some bones join together as we grow.
std: Adults have about 206 bones, but newborns have around 300; many fuse together as the body grows.

ja: 心臓は1日に約10万回、一生では30億回近く拍動する。
easy: Your heart beats about 100,000 times a day. In a lifetime, that is close to three billion times.
std: The heart beats about 100,000 times a day, adding up to nearly three billion beats over a lifetime.

ja: 人の体の約60%は水。脳は約75%が水でできている。
easy: About 60% of your body is water. Your brain is about 75% water.
std: Water makes up about 60% of the adult human body, and about 75% of the brain.

ja: 指紋は一卵性双生児でも同じにならない。同じDNAを持っていても、おなかの中での環境で模様が変わる。
easy: Even twins with the same genes do not have the same fingerprints.
std: Even identical twins, who share the same DNA, have different fingerprints, because the patterns form under slightly different conditions in the womb.

ja: 人の鼻は1兆種類以上のにおいをかぎ分けられるという研究がある（この数字には異論もある）。
easy: One study says people can tell apart more than a trillion smells. Not all scientists agree.
std: A 2014 study suggested humans can distinguish over a trillion odors, although other researchers have questioned the figure.

ja: 人の体の血管をすべてつなげると約10万km。地球を2周半するほどの長さになる。
easy: If you put all the blood tubes in your body end to end, they would go around the Earth about two and a half times.
std: Laid end to end, the blood vessels in an adult body would stretch about 100,000 km, roughly two and a half times around Earth.

ja: ゆっくり深呼吸すると、心拍数が下がり、気持ちが落ち着きやすくなる。
easy: Taking slow, deep breaths can make your heart slow down and help you feel calm.
std: Slow, deep breathing can lower the heart rate and help the body relax.

ja: 眠っている間、脳では老廃物を流し出すしくみが活発になると考えられている。
easy: Scientists think the brain cleans itself while we sleep.
std: Research suggests that during sleep the brain clears out waste products more actively, one of many reasons sleep matters.

ja: 1つの細胞のDNAを伸ばすと約2m。体じゅうのDNAをつなげると、地球と太陽の間を何百回も往復できる長さになる。
easy: The DNA in one cell is about two meters long. All the DNA in your body could go to the sun and back hundreds of times.
std: The DNA in a single human cell would stretch about two meters; all the DNA in the body could reach the Sun and back hundreds of times.

ja: 目に光が入ってから脳が「見えた」と感じるまでには、0.1秒ほどの遅れがある。
easy: It takes about one tenth of a second for your brain to understand what your eyes see.
std: There is a delay of roughly a tenth of a second between light reaching the eye and the brain becoming aware of what it sees.

ja: 皮膚は人体で最大の臓器。大人の皮膚を広げると約1.7m²、畳1枚分ほどになる。
easy: Your skin is the biggest part of your body. Spread out, it would be as big as a small bed.
std: Skin is the body's largest organ; an adult's skin covers about 1.7 square meters.

ja: 人とチンパンジーのDNAは約98.7%が共通している。
easy: About 98.7% of human DNA is the same as chimpanzee DNA.
std: Humans and chimpanzees share about 98.7% of their DNA sequence.

ja: くしゃみの飛まつは、最大で7〜8m先まで飛ぶことがあるという研究がある。
easy: A study found that tiny drops from a sneeze can fly up to eight meters.
std: Research at MIT found that the cloud of droplets from a sneeze can travel up to seven or eight meters.

ja: 歯のエナメル質は体の中で最もかたい組織。骨よりかたいが、一度失われると自然には元に戻らない。
easy: The outside of your teeth is the hardest part of your body. But once it is lost, it does not grow back.
std: Tooth enamel is the hardest substance in the human body, harder than bone, but once lost it cannot grow back.

ja: ハチミツはとても腐りにくい。古代エジプトの墓から見つかったハチミツが、何千年もたっても腐っていなかったと伝えられる。
easy: Honey almost never goes bad. Honey found in very old Egyptian tombs was still fine to eat.
std: Honey hardly ever spoils; pots found in ancient Egyptian tombs were reportedly still edible after thousands of years.

ja: アボカドは植物学では「ベリー（液果）」の仲間に分類される。
easy: In science, an avocado is a kind of berry.
std: Botanically, an avocado is classified as a large berry with a single seed.

ja: ニンジンはもともと紫や黄色が中心だった。今のオレンジ色の品種は、17世紀ごろオランダで広まった。
easy: Long ago, most carrots were purple or yellow. Orange carrots became popular in the Netherlands in the 1600s.
std: Early cultivated carrots were mostly purple or yellow; the orange varieties we know spread from the Netherlands in the 17th century.

ja: チョコレートの原料のカカオ豆は、アステカなどでお金として使われていた。
easy: Long ago in Mexico, people used cacao beans, the beans for chocolate, as money.
std: The Aztecs and other peoples of Mesoamerica used cacao beans, the raw material of chocolate, as currency.

ja: コーヒー豆は、コーヒーチェリーという果実の種。コーヒーの木はエチオピアが原産とされる。
easy: A coffee bean is the seed of a red fruit. The coffee plant first came from Ethiopia.
std: A coffee bean is the seed of a fruit called a coffee cherry, and the coffee plant is native to Ethiopia.

ja: ナポリで生まれたピザは、もともと労働者の手軽な食べ物だった。マルゲリータは王妃の名前にちなむと伝えられる。
easy: Pizza began in Naples as cheap food for working people. The pizza Margherita is said to be named after a queen.
std: Pizza began in Naples as cheap street food for workers, and the Margherita is said to be named after Queen Margherita of Italy.

ja: とうがらしの辛さの単位「スコヴィル値」は1912年に考えられた。純粋なカプサイシンは1600万スコヴィル。
easy: A way to measure how hot a pepper is was made in 1912. The hottest pure part of a pepper scores 16 million.
std: The Scoville scale for chili heat was devised in 1912; pure capsaicin rates about 16 million Scoville units.

ja: イチゴの赤い部分は、植物学では花の付け根（花托）がふくらんだもの。表面の小さな粒の一つ一つが本当の果実。
easy: The red part of a strawberry is not really the fruit. The small seeds on the outside are the real fruits.
std: The red flesh of a strawberry is a swollen part of the flower base; each tiny 'seed' on its surface is actually a separate fruit.

ja: わさびの辛みは、すりおろした直後が最も強く、時間がたつと飛んで弱くなる。
easy: Wasabi is hottest right after you make it. The hot taste goes away after a while.
std: Freshly grated wasabi is at its most pungent right away; its sharp flavor fades as the compounds evaporate over several minutes.

ja: 約3800年前のメソポタミアには、ビールづくりの歌（ニンカシ讃歌）が残っている。最古級のレシピのひとつとされる。
easy: A song from about 3,800 years ago tells how to make beer. It is one of the oldest cooking notes in the world.
std: The Hymn to Ninkasi, written in Mesopotamia about 3,800 years ago, describes beer brewing and is one of the oldest known recipes.

ja: 英語の salary（給料）は、ラテン語の sal（塩）に由来する。ただし「兵士の給料が塩で払われた」という話ははっきりした証拠がない。
easy: The English word salary comes from the Latin word for salt. But the story that soldiers were paid in salt may not be true.
std: The word 'salary' comes from Latin sal, meaning salt, although the popular story that Roman soldiers were paid in salt lacks firm evidence.

ja: 人の遺伝子の約60%は、バナナにも似た働きをする遺伝子がある。生き物の基本のしくみは共通している。
easy: Many of our genes have a similar gene in bananas. All living things share some basic parts.
std: About 60% of human genes have a recognizable counterpart in the banana genome, a reminder that life shares basic machinery.

ja: パイナップルにはブロメラインという酵素が入っていて、肉をやわらかくする。食べると舌がピリピリするのもこのため。
easy: Pineapple can make meat soft. That is also why your tongue can feel strange when you eat a lot of it.
std: Pineapple contains bromelain, an enzyme that breaks down protein, which is why it tenderizes meat and can make your tongue tingle.

ja: 学習のあとにカフェインをとると、記憶の定着を助ける可能性を示した研究がある。
easy: One study found that coffee after learning may help you remember things better.
std: A 2014 study found that caffeine taken after studying images helped people remember them better a day later.

ja: セルビアのロバのミルクで作るチーズ「プレ」は世界一高価なチーズのひとつで、1kgで約1000ユーロ（約16万円）する。
easy: A cheese made from donkey milk in Serbia is one of the most expensive cheeses in the world.
std: Pule, a Serbian cheese made from donkey milk, is among the world's most expensive, selling for around 1,000 euros per kilogram.

ja: 人類が農業を始めたのは約1万年前。それより前の長い歴史のほとんどは狩りと採集の暮らしだった。
easy: People started farming about 10,000 years ago. Before that, people hunted animals and picked plants for food.
std: Humans began farming about 10,000 years ago; for most of our history before that, people lived as hunter-gatherers.

ja: ブルーベリーの青紫色はアントシアニンという色素によるもの。ポリフェノールの一種。
easy: Blueberries get their blue color from a natural color called anthocyanin.
std: Blueberries owe their deep blue color to anthocyanins, a group of plant pigments.

ja: 「うま味」は1908年に日本の池田菊苗が見つけた。2000年代に舌の受容体が見つかり、5番目の基本味として広く認められた。
easy: Umami was found by a Japanese scientist in 1908. Today it is called the fifth basic taste.
std: Umami was identified by Japanese chemist Kikunae Ikeda in 1908 and became widely accepted as the fifth basic taste after taste receptors for it were found in the 2000s.

ja: 砂糖がぜいたく品からふだんの食品になったのは、17〜18世紀のカリブ海の植民地での大量生産から。その裏には奴隷労働の歴史がある。
easy: Sugar was once a luxury. It became common after it was grown in large amounts in the Caribbean, often by slaves.
std: Sugar turned from luxury into everyday food in the 17th and 18th centuries through plantations in the Caribbean, which depended on enslaved labor.

ja: 卵には人に必要なアミノ酸がそろっていて「完全栄養食」とも呼ばれる。ただしビタミンCは含まない。
easy: Eggs have almost everything your body needs, but they have no vitamin C.
std: Eggs contain all the essential amino acids and many vitamins, but they have no vitamin C.

ja: にせの薬だと知らされていても、効果を感じることがある（オープンラベル・プラセボ）という研究がある。
easy: Some people feel better even when they know their medicine is not real.
std: Studies of 'open-label placebos' suggest some people feel better even when told their pills contain no active drug.

ja: 夢中になって時間を忘れる「フロー」の状態では、力を最大限に発揮しやすい。心理学者チクセントミハイが名づけた。
easy: When you are fully into an activity and forget the time, it is called 'flow'. People often do their best work then.
std: In a state of 'flow', people become so absorbed that they lose track of time and often perform at their best; the term was coined by Mihaly Csikszentmihalyi.

ja: 「つり橋効果」：揺れる橋の上のドキドキを、相手への好意と取り違えることがあるという有名な実験がある。
easy: A famous study found that people on a shaking bridge may mistake their fast heartbeat for love.
std: A famous 1974 experiment suggested that people on a frightening suspension bridge may mistake their racing heart for attraction.

ja: ツァイガルニク効果：終わっていない作業は、終わった作業より思い出しやすいとされる。ドラマの「続く」が気になるのもこのため。
easy: We often remember unfinished tasks better than finished ones. That is why we want to know what happens next in a TV drama.
std: The Zeigarnik effect suggests people remember unfinished tasks better than completed ones, one reason cliffhangers keep us watching.

ja: ダニング＝クルーガー効果：ある分野に不慣れな人ほど自分の力を高く見積もり、得意な人ほど低く見積もりがち。
easy: People who are new to something often think they are better than they are. Experts often think they are worse.
std: The Dunning-Kruger effect describes how people with little skill in an area tend to overestimate it, while experts tend to underestimate theirs.

ja: ピグマリオン効果：期待をかけられた人は、その期待に近い成果を出しやすいという考え。
easy: When people expect a lot from you, you may do better. This is called the Pygmalion effect.
std: The Pygmalion effect is the idea that higher expectations from others can lead people to perform better.

ja: 作業が中断されると、元の作業に集中し直すまでに平均20分以上かかるという研究がある。
easy: A study found that after you stop work to do something else, it can take over 20 minutes to get back to it.
std: Research on office workers found that after an interruption it took on average over 20 minutes to return to the original task.

ja: 24時間眠らずにいると、判断力は血中アルコール濃度0.1%で酔ったときと同じくらいまで落ちるという研究がある。
easy: If you stay awake for 24 hours, your mind works about as badly as if you were drunk.
std: Research suggests that staying awake for 24 hours impairs performance about as much as a blood alcohol level of 0.1%.

ja: テトリス効果：同じ作業を長く続けると、夢や頭の中にその動きのパターンが出てくることがある。
easy: After you play a game for a long time, you may see it in your dreams. This is called the Tetris effect.
std: The Tetris effect is when people who spend long periods on an activity start to see its patterns in their thoughts and dreams.

ja: カラーバス効果：ある色やものを意識すると、急にそれが目につくようになる。
easy: When you start to think about the color red, you suddenly see red things everywhere.
std: Once you start paying attention to something, such as a color or a car model, you suddenly notice it everywhere.

ja: 確証バイアス：人は自分の考えに合う情報ばかり集めてしまいがち。
easy: People like to find facts that agree with what they already believe.
std: Confirmation bias is the tendency to seek out and favor information that supports what we already believe.

ja: 返報性の原理：何かをもらうと、お返しをしなければと感じやすい。多くの文化に見られる心理。
easy: When someone gives us something, we want to give something back. This is true in many cultures.
std: The norm of reciprocity, the feeling that we should return favors, appears in cultures all over the world.

ja: 大人になると時間が速く過ぎるように感じる。新しい経験が減るためという説がある。
easy: Time seems to go faster as we get older. One idea is that we have fewer new experiences.
std: Time often seems to speed up as we age; one explanation is that we have fewer novel experiences to mark the passing days.

ja: プルースト効果：においは、昔の記憶や気持ちを強く思い出させる。
easy: A smell can bring back an old memory very strongly.
std: Smells can trigger vivid memories and emotions from the past, sometimes called the Proust effect.

ja: 音楽を聞くと、人は自然とリズムに体を合わせようとする。
easy: When we hear music, our bodies want to move with the beat.
std: When people hear music, they naturally tend to synchronize their movements with the beat, a process called entrainment.

ja: 系列位置効果：一覧の最初と最後の項目は、真ん中より覚えやすい。
easy: In a list, it is easier to remember the first and last things than the ones in the middle.
std: The serial-position effect means we tend to remember the first and last items in a list better than those in the middle.

ja: 笑いは人どうしの絆を強める役割をもつと考えられている。チンパンジーなどの類人猿も遊びの中で笑う。
easy: Laughing helps people feel close. Apes like chimpanzees also laugh when they play.
std: Laughter is thought to help strengthen social bonds, and great apes such as chimpanzees also laugh during play.

ja: 最初のコンピューターウイルスとされる「Creeper」（1971年）は、こわすためではなく実験として作られたものだった。
easy: One of the first computer viruses, made in 1971, was only a test. It did not try to hurt computers.
std: Creeper, often called the first computer virus, was written in 1971 as an experiment and did no damage.

ja: 世界初のウェブサイトは1991年にCERNのティム・バーナーズ＝リーが公開した。今もそのページを見ることができる。
easy: The first website was made in 1991. You can still visit it today.
std: Tim Berners-Lee published the first website at CERN in 1991, and a copy of it is still online today.

ja: 地球のまわりでは1万基以上の人工衛星が動いていて、使われなくなった衛星やかけら（宇宙ごみ）はさらに多い。
easy: More than 10,000 working machines go around the Earth in space. There is even more space trash.
std: More than 10,000 active satellites now orbit Earth, along with far more pieces of space debris.

ja: 1947年、ハーバード大学のコンピューターに本物の虫（ガ）がはさまり、「バグ」として記録に残った。
easy: In 1947, a real insect got stuck inside a computer. People wrote it down as a 'bug'.
std: In 1947, engineers found a moth trapped in the Harvard Mark II computer and taped it into their log as the 'first actual case of bug being found'.

ja: 電子レンジは1945年、レーダーの技術者がポケットのチョコレートが溶けたことに気づいたのがきっかけで生まれた。
easy: The microwave oven was invented when an engineer saw that a chocolate bar in his pocket had melted.
std: The microwave oven was invented after engineer Percy Spencer noticed that a chocolate bar in his pocket melted near radar equipment in 1945.

ja: GPSはもともと軍事用の技術。1983年の大韓航空機撃墜事件のあと、民間でも使えるようにすると発表された。
easy: GPS was first made for the army. After a plane was shot down in 1983, the US said everyone could use it.
std: GPS began as a military system; after Korean Air Lines Flight 007 was shot down in 1983, the US announced it would be opened to civilian use.

ja: 初代プレイステーションは1994年に日本で発売された。CD-ROMを使い、ゲームの表現を大きく変えた。
easy: The first PlayStation came out in Japan in 1994. It used CDs and changed video games.
std: The original PlayStation launched in Japan in 1994, and its use of CD-ROMs helped transform video games.

ja: 1971年、レイ・トムリンソンが初めてネットワークで電子メールを送った。相手は隣に置いた別のコンピューターだった。
easy: The first email was sent in 1971. It went to a computer right next to the sender.
std: Ray Tomlinson sent the first network email in 1971, between two computers sitting side by side.

ja: ディープラーニングの基本的な考え方は1980年代からあったが、計算機の力が足りず、広く使われたのは2010年代になってから。
easy: The main ideas of deep learning were around in the 1980s. But computers were too slow to use them well until the 2010s.
std: Key ideas behind deep learning existed in the 1980s, but they only took off in the 2010s, when computers became powerful enough.

ja: Wi-Fiという名前には特別な意味はない。Hi-Fiに似せて作ったブランド名。
easy: The name Wi-Fi does not mean anything. It was made to sound like 'hi-fi'.
std: The name Wi-Fi doesn't stand for anything; it was a brand name created to sound like 'hi-fi'.

ja: 合言葉（パスワード）は2000年以上前の古代ローマ軍でも使われていた。夜の見張りで仲間を見分けるため。
easy: Over 2,000 years ago, Roman soldiers used secret words at night to know who was a friend.
std: More than 2,000 years ago, Roman soldiers used watchwords at night to tell friend from enemy, an early form of the password.

ja: Netflixは1997年、DVDを郵送で貸し出す会社として始まった。ネット配信を始めたのは2007年。
easy: Netflix started in 1997 by sending DVDs by mail. It started streaming in 2007.
std: Netflix was founded in 1997 as a DVD-by-mail rental service and only began streaming video in 2007.

ja: リチウムイオン電池を開発した吉野彰は、2019年にノーベル化学賞を受けた。スマートフォンの普及を支えた技術。
easy: Akira Yoshino helped make the battery in your phone. He won the Nobel Prize in 2019.
std: Akira Yoshino shared the 2019 Nobel Prize in Chemistry for developing the lithium-ion battery, which powers today's smartphones.
